newsitem.title: USA: Forest Oil stake to grow at JEDI.
newsitem.headline: Forest Oil stake to grow at JEDI.

text.p: Forest Oil Corp said the Joint Energy Development Investments LP (JEDI) signed a letter of intent to buy two million shares of Forest common stock at $14.75 per share for a total of $29.5 million.
JEDI is a Delaware limited partnership, whose general partner is an affiliate of Enron.

The deal is contingent on Anschutz Corp converting its Forest preferred stock and exercising certain warrants it currently holds to purchase common stock for a total of $15.3 million, Forest Oil said.

The deal also hinges on the signing of a definitive agreement. In addition, the parties can choose to call off the deal if the 10-day average closing price per share of Forest stock is less than $14.00 or more than $15.50.
JEDI purchase would bring its ownership to 3.68 million shares, or 12.1 percent, of the outstanding shares of Forest.
The newly purchased shares would be non-transferable by JEDI, except in limited circumstances, until May 31, 1997, Forest Oil said.

Anschutz would convert 100 percent of the Second Series convertible preferred stock, with a liquidation preference of $11.16 million, into common stock. Anschutz would also exercise 388,888, or 10 percent of the outstanding warrants it holds, for a total exercise price of about $4.1 million.

The Anschutz transactions would bring the total common stock held by Anschutz to 7.64 million shares, or 25 percent of the outstanding shares of Forest. The term of the remaining 3.5 million warrants owned by Anschutz would be extended 12 months to July 27, 1999, Forest Oil said.

The company would use the proceeds from the sale of equity and the warrant exercise, plus about $9.5 million in bank debt, to extinguish about $43 million of debt owed to JEDI currently bearing interest at 12-1/2 percent.

Forest said it estimates primary shares outstanding would total 30.5 million and fully diluted shares would total 36.7 million after the conversion. Forest estimates primary shares before the transactions to total 26.9 million and fully diluted shares to total 34.7 million.

In a statement accompanying the press release, David Keyte, chief financial officer, said: "As a result of these transactions, Forest's leverage would be reduced to about 40 percent on a book basis and 25 percent on a market (capitalization) basis and cash flow and earnings would increase by about $4.7 million per year.
"In January, when we completed our public offering, we told our investors that our short-term leverage target was 40% of book capitalization.

"We have now achieved that target with a two-million-share equity issuance at a 34 percent premium to our public offering price. This transaction would add significant financial flexibility to Forest and simplify its balance sheet considerably," Keyte said.
